claim: Technology-only licensing (MD-6) transfers ~53 residual minutes per account-year to the sponsor at x1.4 efficiency; its lower vendor cost is a transfer, not a saving (system variable $197 vs $167 AI-native)
Informational and neutral BMF changes (~99.8% of monthly changes) can be eliminated as work by a field-and-direction materiality table; a naive any-change rule creates ~585x more reviews

IRS BMF, Pub 78 and auto-revocation are full monthly snapshots that overwrite history and must be diffed and archived; OFAC publishes public delta files but a full reload on change is safer; trade.gov CSL is a daily full file at 05:00 ET; SAM exclusions is a daily full active-set extract; the 990 XML series is incremental by batch
No national state charity-registration dataset exists; California exposes delinquency through a per-organisation lookup; most state registry change detection cannot be automated from bulk data
notes: Absence of a bulk list on the CA page is not proof none exists

notes: Direction Medium; levels Low until replay and renewal-failure measurements

claim: Public-intelligence maintenance is ~96% of single-sponsor registry cost; sponsor-specific decisions are ~$4.3k per sponsor-year; the marginal cost of an added sponsor is ~$3-24k a year (base) driven mainly by its addition to the shared charity union

A zero-acceptance attribute sample of 149 per stratum detects a systematic error rate of 2% or more with 95% confidence; demonstrating rates below 0.1% needs ~2995 samples, so sample audits complement but cannot replace deterministic release-time controls
notes: Standard binomial attribute sampling; auditor acceptance untested (V-9)
